text.arabic_uthmani: أَوْ خَلْقًۭا مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِى صُدُورِكُمْ ۚ فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَن يُعِيدُنَا ۖ قُلِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ ۚ فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ ۖ قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبًۭا

words.gloss_range: disjunctive alternative carrying the prior imperative list into an open final option
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:aw}}) begins 17:51 in the middle of the prior command frame, carrying the implied "be" from 17:50 into one more alternative. Its disjunction is not hesitation; it broadens stones and iron into a final open challenge. The particle therefore makes the verse boundary itself part of the argument, moving from named hard materials to whatever created form the addressees can imagine as greatest.

topics.headline: suspended disjunction across the verse boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:51 does not start from zero; it continues the material dare already begun in 17:50.
topics.reason: QAC and local syntax treat the particle as a disjunctive continuation of the prior implied imperative rather than a new independent clause.

topics.headline: third alternative opens the challenge beyond named materials
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the challenge widen from stones and iron into any imagined created thing, which prepares the move from material impossibility to agency and timing.
topics.reason: The following accusative creation phrase depends on the earlier command frame, and the row family tracks how the boundary converts the material list into dialogue about restoration.

words.gloss_range: indefinite createdness as any imagined resistant created kind, with measured shaping in view and fabrication branches only background range
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes creating, measuring or shaping, and in other contexts fabricating; here the local predicate selects genuine createdness under the resurrection challenge
words.prose: {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) is accusative under the carried command, so it names the final thing they might imagine becoming. Its indefiniteness opens the category: not one named material, but any created kind they think most resistant. The word recalls the nearby resurrection-denial phrase "new creation" (17:49; 17:98) while dropping the newness modifier, so the issue widens to createdness itself. The creation root keeps measured constitution in view, while the nearby answer will shift from createdness to first origination.

topics.headline: indefinite accusative createdness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is not a detached object but the open final predicate of the earlier challenge.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as an indefinite accusative predicate under the implied prior command.

topics.headline: measured createdness without importing fabrication as local sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels that even the most formidable imagined form remains inside createdness, while the fabrication branch is only part of the wider root range.
topics.reason: The local resurrection challenge selects genuine createdness and measured shaping; the broader fabricate sense is valid root range but not the local sense.

topics.headline: createdness framed by return and first origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word recalls resurrection-denial wording nearby (17:49; 17:98) while widening from new creation to createdness as such.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete nearby references, and the local phrase omits the newness adjective while keeping the creation term active in the same resurrection argument.

words.gloss_range: compound from/of whatever, making the source domain unrestricted and relative rather than interrogative
words.prose: {{ar:مِّمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) turns the final alternative into a selection from whatever looms large for the addressees. The compound is relative, not a question, and its partitive force keeps the challenge open-ended. It binds the creation term to the following inner-magnitude clause rather than leaving it as a generic created thing.

topics.headline: from whatever as open relative domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase gives the addressees the widest possible field from which to imagine resistance.
topics.reason: QAC treats the form as min plus relative pronoun, and the local clause confirms a relative, not interrogative, reading.

topics.headline: relative bridge to subjective magnitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the imagined creation is defined by what grows large inside them, not by an objective catalogue of materials.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence places the phrase at the head of the relative clause completed by the inner-magnitude predicate.

words.gloss_range: intransitive ongoing greatness or formidability located in the addressees inner estimation
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers greatness, magnitude, rank, age, arrogance, and magnification; here Form I intransitive selects perceived greatness in an inner evaluative field
words.prose: {{ar:يَكْبُرُ}} ({{tr:yakburu}}) makes the imagined thing continuously loom large rather than being made large by an agent. Its singular agreement keeps the greatness attached to the relative "whatever," and the following chest phrase makes that greatness subjective. The inner-magnitude pattern also resonates with what chests conceal as greater still (3:118) and with arrogance in chests (40:56), while this local form remains perceived magnitude rather than an arrogance verb. The word therefore shifts the dare from objective hardness to the addressees own measure of what feels impossible.

topics.headline: intransitive imperfect greatness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the thing simply looms in their evaluative field; no one is making it great inside the clause.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form I imperfect without a direct object and with the relative pronoun as subject.

topics.headline: greatness measured inside the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the test uses the deniers own sense of formidability against them.
topics.reason: The local prepositional phrase places the magnitude in their chests, and contextual rows support an inner-evaluation cluster.

topics.headline: surah-wide greatness range localized here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a broader greatness field in the surah, while this occurrence stays with perceived magnitude rather than arrogance or magnification forms.
topics.reason: The rows compare related greatness domains, but local morphology selects simple intransitive greatness in this clause.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition marking the inner container where the imagined magnitude is held
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) places the greatness inside the addressees, not out in the object itself. With the chest noun, the ordinary locative becomes psychological containment: the challenge targets what their own inner estimation holds as too great. The phrase completes the predicate, making the whole imagined creation opponent-indexed.

topics.headline: locative interiority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scale of impossibility is located inside the deniers themselves.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the preposition govern the chest phrase as the local domain of greatness.

topics.headline: prepositional tail completes subjective predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the phrase cannot be omitted without flattening the challenge into generic size.
topics.reason: The local syntax completes the relative clause with the prepositional phrase, turning greatness into an inner criterion.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed chests as the collective inner field from which estimation and later speech issue
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes chest, front, source, issuing forth, and outward emergence; here it names possessed chests as an expressible inner domain
words.prose: {{ar:صُدُورِكُمْ}} ({{tr:ṣudūrikum}}) fixes the imagined magnitude in the addressees own collective interior. The plural and suffix distribute the scale across them as a group, while the root range of front or source lets the later objections feel as though they issue outward from this inner field. It is chests rather than hearts, an accessible layer of interiority that can become speech and gesture. The recurring "what is in your chests" frame (3:29; 3:154; 5:7) is inverted here into their own criterion of greatness, and the suffix keeps them addressed as you just before they become the predicted they.

topics.headline: plural possessed chests as evaluative field

topics.reason: QAC identifies the plural possessed noun as genitive after the preposition, not as an actor or object.

topics.headline: chest as source of outward objection

topics.reason: The root range supports source or issuing pressure, and the subsequent speech clauses realize that pressure without changing the local noun sense.

topics.headline: outer interiority rather than hidden hearts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah uses an expressible interior field, and the direct address persists just before the deniers are narrated as they.
topics.reason: The rows contrast chest language with heart language and note recurring chest formulas; locally the suffix keeps direct address active before the narrative displacement.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector in the first forecast, linking the imagined challenge to predicted speech
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the challenge into an immediate predicted response. Joined to the future-marked speech verb, it does not merely add the next clause; it makes their objection the consequence of the dare. This first connector also sets up the later matching forecast of gesture.

topics.headline: first consequent forecast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deniers response is forecast as the direct uptake of the challenge, not simply reported narration.
topics.reason: QAC identifies this connector as immediate sequence in the first fa-sa construction, and the later matching construction confirms the paired forecast pattern.

words.gloss_range: future-marked denier speech as the first predicted objection in a controlled dialogue
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers saying, speech, assertion, and commanded utterance; here the sa-prefixed imperfect selects foretold denier speech
words.prose: {{ar:سَيَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:sayaqūlūna}}) places the first objection under foreknowledge before it is uttered. The common speech root becomes part of a tightly controlled exchange: predicted objection, commanded answer, renewed objection, commanded answer. So the agency question is not neutral narration; it is the first denier speech turn inside a divine forecast.

topics.headline: sa-prefixed predicted speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears their objection as already anticipated before they speak it.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the sa-prefixed imperfect, and the contextual rows place it in a polemical speech environment.

topics.headline: first of the ayahs alternating speech turns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah as a two-cycle dialogue rather than a single question and answer.
topics.reason: The row family tracks the four speech markers that alternate denier objections and commanded replies.

words.gloss_range: personal interrogative subject asking who can restore, not how restoration works or when it occurs
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) makes the first objection an agency question. The deniers ask who restores us, not how restoration works, and that form prepares an answer that begins with the relative "the one who." It also sets the first half of the ayahs paired interrogatives: who is answered by origination, while when is answered by modal nearness.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the objection is about agency before it is about process or timing.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as interrogative subject of the restoration verb.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the argument move from agency to schedule through two matched questions.
topics.reason: The row family links this first interrogative with the later temporal interrogative and the two commanded answers.

words.gloss_range: caused restoration of us as a pending disputed action, with return/repetition pressure tied to first occurrence
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes return, recurrence, repetition, custom, and related cyclic return senses; here Form IV selects causing the speakers to return/restored
words.prose: {{ar:يُعِيدُنَا}} ({{tr:yuʿīdunā}}) makes the speakers themselves the object to be restored. Form IV turns return into caused restoration, and the imperfect keeps the act pending inside their challenge. The root range of return and recurrence matters because the answer will point to the first occurrence: restoration is measured against origination rather than invented as a new impossibility.

topics.reason: QAC identifies the Form IV imperfect as transitive with an object, supporting a causative restoration reading.

topics.reason: The local verb selects restoration; broader recurrence senses help the proof pattern, and concrete beginning-restoring parallels such as 10:4 and 10:34 support that pattern without replacing the local sense.

words.gloss_range: commanded prophetic reply to the agency question, with liaison-marked surface before the following relative answer
words.root_gloss_range: local root record is tied to the imperative speech form in this bundle; the word functions as commanded utterance rather than a lexical noun range
words.prose: {{ar:قُلِ}} ({{tr:quli}}) shifts the scene from denier question to commanded prophetic reply. The answer is not left as speculation; it is transmitted as instruction, like nearby commanded counter-argument speech in 17:42. Its liaison vowel belongs to the following definite relative, while the repeated command structure divides the ayah into two matched answers: one for who restores and one for when.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply is authorized commanded speech, not the Prophets independent speculation.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a second-person imperative addressed to the Prophet, and the cited nearby commanded-speech argument (17:42) supports the refutation pattern.

topics.reason: QAC notes the liaison kasra before the following definite relative, and the later bare command creates a parallel answer pair.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun answering who by identifying the agent through a defining act
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) answers the who-question by saying "the one who" rather than giving a bare title. The implied subject is compressed, so the relative pronoun strikes directly as the answer-predicate. It identifies the restorer through the defining act that follows: first origination.

topics.headline: relative pronoun identifies the agent by action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that agency is answered through a deed of origination, not through an abstract label.
topics.reason: QAC treats the word as a masculine singular relative pronoun introducing the identifying clause, and the row family explains the implied answer structure.

words.gloss_range: completed direct origination of you, with split-origination pressure answering the restoration challenge
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes splitting, cleaving, originating, natural disposition, and fissure imagery; here Form I perfect selects completed origination of the addressees
words.prose: {{ar:فَطَرَكُمْ}} ({{tr:faṭarakum}}) returns the speakers from us to you and grounds the answer in a completed first act. The verb does not merely repeat createdness; it reaches to origination, with splitting-open pressure behind the root. That deeper first act becomes the proof for restoration: the one who originated you the first time is the answer to who can cause return. The same the-one-who-originated argument pattern appears in other prophetic scenes (6:79; 11:51), so the local answer joins a wider proof tradition without leaving this direct address.

topics.reason: QAC identifies the Form I perfect with second-person plural object, grounding the answer in completed origination.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels origination as a more primal act than generic making, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as originating the addressees.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports splitting or cleaving pressure, but the local transitive perfect selects origination rather than a literal physical split.

topics.reason: Concrete alladhī-faṭara argument scenes (6:79; 11:51) and the local creation-return sequence support the row familys proof-chain reading.

words.gloss_range: first as a bound temporal adverb in the first-time proof phrase
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes firstness, precedence, beginning, and return-to-origin pressure; here the construct phrase selects the first occurrence as temporal precedent
words.prose: {{ar:أَوَّلَ}} ({{tr:awwala}}) binds firstness to the following instance noun, making the answer point to a precise temporal precedent: the first time. words.gloss_range: indefinite instance noun completing first time as a countable occurrence

words.prose: {{ar:مَرَّةٍۢ}} ({{tr:marratin}}) completes the phrase as one indefinite instance: a first time. topics.reason: The local phrase selects instance or occurrence; the concrete surah references support recurrence of counting language without importing unrelated root branches.

words.gloss_range: second consequential connector, moving from the answer to a predicted bodily reaction
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moves the scene from the originator answer to the deniers visible reaction. This second fa-sa pattern mirrors the earlier forecast, but now the forecast escalates from speech to body and then back to speech.

words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on head motion, shaking or nodding, repeated agitation, and commotion; here Form IV selects causing their heads to move as a predicted response
words.prose: {{ar:سَيُنْغِضُونَ}} ({{tr:sayunghiḍūna}}) is the ayahs marked bodily verb. It is future-predicted, transitive, and Form IV, so they are made to cause their heads to move rather than merely tremble. Because the root occurs only here in the Quran, the gesture becomes strange and vivid; its range can hold mockery, disbelief, agitation, or anxious inquiry without forcing one flat gloss. In the larger clause, the rare gesture is directed toward the Prophet and joined to the timing taunt, making the denial bodily and verbal at once.

topics.reason: QAC identifies a sa-prefixed Form IV imperfect governing the head object.

Within Surah 17, the same modal form also appears with mercy (17:8) and praised station (17:79), so this answer belongs to a local gradient of hope and expectation.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle subordinating the being clause after the modal verb
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) makes the final being clause dependent on the modal verb. It triggers the subjunctive and prevents the answer from becoming an independent date-statement. The particle helps stack expectation and grammatical dependency before the final word gives nearness.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive copular being of the implied event, making nearness the predicate rather than naming a concrete action
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers being, becoming, existence, occurrence, and copular predication; here the subjunctive copular use predicates nearness of the implied resurrection event
words.prose: {{ar:يَكُونَ}} ({{tr:yakūna}}) supplies being for the implied event after the modal particle. The answer does not say the event comes, returns, or strikes; it says that it may be near. This basic being verb also shifts the passage from the opponents imagined becoming in 17:50 to the event whose nearness is governed by divine timing. Near the next instruction turn (17:53), the same being-and-commanded-speech environment moves from resurrection doctrine to conduct, sharpening the control shift here.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative predicate of nearness, answering when with imminent proximity rather than a fixed date
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes nearness in time, space, relation, kinship, approaching, and in other forms offering or drawing near; here it selects temporal nearness with broader proximity pressure
words.prose: {{ar:قَرِيبًۭا}} ({{tr:qarīban}}) closes the ayah by predicating nearness, not by supplying the date that was demanded. Its indefiniteness leaves the degree unstated: near, soon, but not calendared. The root can carry spatial and relational proximity as well, while the local timing question selects temporal imminence; maximum imagined material challenge ends with minimal temporal disclosure. The modal-nearness construction also has an eschatological parallel in 7:185, so the final word is formulaic nearness rather than an empty evasion.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction "mimma yakburu fi sudurikum" attaches magnitude to what becomes great in the hearers' breasts, while "khalqan" keeps even that extreme inside createdness.
baseline_models.mechanism: The hypothetical escalation does not search for a substance outside creative power. It exposes a scale generated in the interior: an imagined material becomes prohibitive because the breast magnifies it, although creation remains measured and originated.

activation_trace.role: The image of measuring a thing supplies the bounded created category against which imagined impossibility is tested.
Magnifying something in the breast literally locates the scale of the obstacle in the hearers' appraisal.
The interior source from which actions issue makes the magnified objection a generative posture, not a neutral material fact.

changed_reading.before: The challenge merely asks the skeptics to name an objectively harder substance.
changed_reading.after: The challenge relocates impossibility into what they themselves magnify inwardly; even their maximal counterexample remains a measured creation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: "Who will restore us?" is answered by the one who opened their existence the first time, and the exchange closes by bringing the event temporally near.
baseline_models.mechanism: Return is presented as a reversible path already demonstrated by origination. The first occurrence is both a beginning and, through the split branch of counting recurrence and the branch of outcome, a template whose trajectory can be run to its return.

activation_trace.role: Return after departure and repetition after a beginning supplies the explicit restoration path.
The split mapped image of time being counted and recurring adds a temporal cycle to the restoration.
Origination and inception identify the operative power already evidenced in the addressees.
The branch in which a thing returns to its outcome lets "first" carry an endpoint as well as a beginning.
A bounded occurrence in time makes the first event a repeatable temporal instance rather than an inaccessible absolute.
Temporal approach converts the demonstrated return-path into an impending rather than merely possible event.

changed_reading.before: First creation is only an analogy offered as evidence for a second creation.
changed_reading.after: First origination is an operative return-path: beginning, recurrence, outcome, and approaching time are folded into one mechanism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Four speech turns surround two shifting questions, while the interlocutors direct a head movement toward the speaker.
baseline_models.mechanism: The passage stages a negotiation rather than two isolated requests for information. Once agency is answered by first origination, resistance migrates to timing; the head movement bodily marks that migration, and the second answer converts delay into proximity.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation over an affair organizes the repeated sayings as an adversarial exchange whose objection keeps changing form.
Speech functioning as conjecture marks the questions as speculative resistance rather than straightforward inquiry.
The literal head supplies the bodily surface on which the unresolved objection becomes visible.
Approaching time answers the migrated timing objection without accepting its premise of remoteness.

changed_reading.before: The verse records a question about agency followed by a question about date.
changed_reading.after: It exposes a moving resistance: when the agent-question is closed, disbelief shifts into timing and is answered by nearness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The candidate materials of 17:51 enter a context in which every thing already performs praise although the hearers do not comprehend it. Stone, iron, or a still greater creation therefore cannot function as mute counterexamples to restoration; their apparent muteness diagnoses limited reception.

activation_trace.role: Created existence keeps every proposed material within the same field of origination.
A thing's indication functioning as speech permits material existence itself to contribute a response.
Repeated worshipful praise supplies the active response attributed across the created field.
The unrestricted knowable thing extends that response to every material candidate later proposed.
Negated understanding locates silence in the hearers' failed comprehension rather than in created things.

structural_cues: 17:44 distributes praise across heavens, earth, and every thing before denying the audience comprehension.
17:51 answers human speech while escalating through imagined kinds of creation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies universal praise and failed comprehension; I infer that the materials proposed around 17:51 remain expressive participants rather than mute counterexamples. A live alternative is that 17:44 supplies only a general cosmological backdrop.

changed_reading.before: The skeptics can imagine an inert substance whose nature defeats reanimation.
changed_reading.after: Their supposedly inert counterexamples already participate in an uncomprehended created response, so muteness cannot establish impossibility.

context_deltas.mechanism: The inward magnification of 17:51 becomes one station in a bodily route of refusal: barrier, covered hearts, weighted ears, turned backs, magnifying breasts, and shaking heads. The objection is produced and displayed by an enclosed perceptual posture.

activation_trace.role: The action-producing interior is the focus point where the earlier perceptual closure becomes a magnified objection.
The literal head makes the inward refusal externally legible as bodily response.
Blocked access supplies the outer boundary of the refusal mechanism.
What is enclosed in the self supplies the concealed interior layer through which the message is filtered.
Heaviness in the ear blocks reception before the objection is articulated.
Turning the back extends perceptual closure into overt bodily withdrawal.

structural_cues: The context moves through barrier, heart, ear, and back before 17:51 names breast and head.
The branchless head-shaking verb in 17:51 links inward appraisal to visible motion without requiring an invented citation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a sequence of blocked organs and turned bodies; I infer a causal route from failed reception to inward magnification and then head gesture. The live alternative is a looser accumulation of separate refusal images rather than one bodily circuit.

changed_reading.before: What grows great in their breasts is an isolated intellectual estimate of material difficulty.
changed_reading.after: The estimate is generated within an embodied enclosure that blocks reception, magnifies the obstacle, and discharges refusal through the head.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate context lays out disintegration, arousal from stillness, newness after severance, created form, stone, and iron. The focus answer turns these from rival substances into traversable states: what can be cut, stilled, hardened, measured, and first opened can be returned.

activation_trace.role: Measurement holds fragmented and hardened forms within one ordered created process.
Return after departure provides the directional reversal across material states.
Opening and splitting supply the transition by which a closed or hard state need not remain terminal.
Pulverization and debris supply the disintegrated endpoint that the skeptics treat as irreversible.
Stirring what is still from its repose supplies the reverse motion out of apparent inertness.
Newness arising after cutting directly joins severance to renewed state.
The requested new creation remains an act of origination rather than a material exception.
Solid stone supplies one extreme state of resistance.
Iron and resistant hardness supply the second extreme without escaping the state cycle.

structural_cues: 17:49 moves from bones and debris to being raised as a new creation; 17:50 then escalates to stone and iron; 17:51 generalizes beyond both.
The reply changes the axis from present material condition to the agency that initiated the first condition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fragmentation, stillness, renewal, stone, iron, measurement, opening, and return; I infer directional transitions among those states under one originating agency. The alternative is that the materials are only escalating examples with no process model.

changed_reading.before: Bones, debris, stone, and iron are separate objections ranked by physical difficulty.
changed_reading.after: They are phases in a reversible material process, and the answer identifies origination rather than hardness as the controlling variable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah converts the focus dialogue into the event it debates: the one who is asked about calls, the questioners answer, and their experienced interval contracts to little. Nearness is therefore enacted as call-response and retrospective temporal compression, not supplied as a calendar date.

activation_trace.role: The negotiated speech in the focus ayah establishes the dialogue that the next ayah turns performative.
Restoration supplies the event realized by the ensuing summons.
Temporal approach is re-expressed as the brevity perceived once the response occurs.
The spoken summons supplies the initiating action that performs the promised restoration.
Answering speech completes the call-response circuit with the formerly questioning hearers.
Duration in a place supplies the interval that is retrospectively reassessed.
Littleness contracts the apparently long wait at the moment of response.

structural_cues: 17:51 ends with an answer about nearness; 17:52 immediately begins with the day of summons and response.
The speakers who ask "when?" become the respondents who estimate that they remained only a little.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a question-answer exchange followed by divine call, human response, and perceived brevity; I infer that 17:52 enacts the mechanism promised in 17:51. The alternative is a simple chronological sequel without deliberate speech-role reversal.

changed_reading.before: "Perhaps it will be near" gives an indefinite estimate of future timing.
changed_reading.after: Nearness is experiential and performative: a summons collapses the debate into response, and the elapsed interval then appears little.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later contrast between powerless invoked figures and seekers of a means to their Lord gives the focus ending a second axis. "Near" remains temporal, but it also resonates with relational approach: restoration returns creatures to the originating one while every alleged intermediary is itself seeking which is nearer.

activation_trace.role: The explicit approach of time anchors the primary temporal reading.
Inability to lift what covers or afflicts removes the invoked figures from controlling the return.
Inability to transform a condition reinforces the agency distinction established by first origination.
Active seeking supplies movement toward the Lord rather than autonomous power in the seekers.
The heart's expectation of what is hoped for gives relational approach an affective orientation.
Nearness opposed to distance supplies the relational counterpart to the focus ayah's temporal nearness.

structural_cues: 17:51 answers "who restores us" with the originator and ends on temporal nearness.
17:56-57 denies transformative control to invoked others and describes those very figures as seeking which is nearer to their Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies temporal nearness in 17:51 and relational nearness amid seeking in 17:57; I infer deliberate resonance between the two axes. The materially live alternative keeps "near" in 17:51 strictly temporal.

changed_reading.before: Nearness in 17:51 concerns only how soon the event may occur.
changed_reading.after: Temporal approach also opens onto relational approach: the return is near in time and directs every dependent claimant toward the sole originating agency.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context frames 17:51 with magnitude: an earlier saying is appraised as enormous, signs warn and test, yet warning increases transgression until it is called great. The focus breast is the conversion point in this feedback loop, where disclosure can be inwardly enlarged into an objection and then outwardly enlarged into conduct.

activation_trace.role: Magnification in the breast names the internal amplification stage of the loop.
The source from which acts issue links inward amplification to later outward transgression.
Appraisal as overwhelming or awe-inducing introduces magnified speech at the opening edge of the context.
Visible signs supply disclosure that should interrupt the objection but instead enters the feedback loop.
Warning by inducing fear supplies the intended pressure exerted by the signs.
Testing a person as metal is tested supplies the transformation point at which disclosure reveals response.
Increase and growth provide the feedback arrow from warning to intensified refusal.
Exceeding the limit in disobedience supplies the outward behavior produced by the amplification.
Great magnitude at the context's closing edge displays the enlarged behavioral output of what grew inwardly.

structural_cues: The window opens with "a tremendous saying," places "what grows great in your breasts" at 17:51, and closes with "great transgression."
17:59-60 moves from visible signs and warning through testing to increase rather than correction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the magnitude frame and the sequence sign, warning, test, increase, and great transgression; I infer that inward magnification is the causal conversion point. An alternative is that the repeated magnitude language is rhetorical framing without a single feedback mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The great thing in their breasts is simply the largest material counterexample they can imagine.
changed_reading.after: It is also an amplification process: warning enters the interior as a test, becomes a magnified objection, and can emerge as still greater transgression.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This uses the form-distant q-l-l target mapped from the repeated q-w-l occurrence, so it must not replace the ordinary speech reading. It remains anchored because the focus ayah repeats that occurrence around an explicit head movement; downstream prose should present it only as a secondary acoustic-bodily resonance.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The four q-w-l occurrences alternate around the branchless head-shaking verb and the literal heads.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant mapped image of disturbance and motion lets repeated speech resonate as bodily destabilization.
The literal head gives the exploratory disturbance a visible bodily carrier.

changed_reading.before: Speech and head-shaking are separate verbal and gestural details.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the repeated speech exchange generates an instability that reverberates into the moving head.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The milk-return, tooth-emergence, and impending-birth branches are remote organic images rather than direct glosses of the focus forms. They remain anchored to three explicit focus roots and converge on latent return becoming imminent; downstream prose should label the model as a material analogy, not an asserted lexical meaning.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: "Fatarakum," "asa," and "qariban" can jointly carry emergence, hoped-for return, and an approaching birth around the explicit restoration question.

activation_trace.role: Return after departure supplies the shared directional core of the organic analogy.
A tooth breaking into emergence supplies a concrete image of latent form crossing a surface.
Hope for milk to return after interruption supplies recoverable capacity rather than creation from inert absence.
Impending birth supplies nearness as pressure toward manifestation.

changed_reading.before: Restoration is imagined only as external reconstruction of dead material.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also resembles latent capacity returning and pressing toward emergence, like renewed lactation, a breaking tooth, or near birth.

strongest_changes: The material challenge shifts from ranking substances to traversing reversible states under the agency of first origination.
The next ayah performs nearness as a call-response event that retrospectively contracts elapsed time.
Nearness acquires a relational resonance when the allegedly powerful are shown seeking which is nearer to their Lord.
The surrounding sequence turns inward magnification into a feedback loop from warning through testing to increased transgression.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah acts as a hinge: created matter is already responsive though unheard, perceptual enclosure converts evidence into inward scale, and the same scale links the context's tremendous speech to its closing great transgression.
remaining_uncertainties: The causal unity of the barrier-heart-ear-back-breast-head route is inferred rather than explicitly stated.
The relational resonance of "near" may be secondary to its plain temporal force.
The unstable-speech and organic-latency outliers depend on deliberately remote branch activations and require explicit qualification.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Whatever looms greatest inwardly is answered by the first split-opening.** `ك ب ر:B003/B010` regards as great and heavy, `ص د ر:B001/B004` is chest and source, `ع و د:B001` returns, and `ف ط ر:B001/B002` splits open and originates. Their imagined maximum is located in chests; the reply relocates causality to the one who first opened form into being. I infer subjective magnitude does not measure originating capacity. Resurrection reads as return by the prior opener.
2. **Head-shaking performs resistance while “near” compresses delay.** `ن غ ض:B001/B002` gives astonished head motion and jolting, `ر ء س:B001/B002` head and leadership, and `ق ر ب:B001/B002` spatial and temporal nearness. I infer bodily dismissal protects their temporal distance; the final answer removes it. The exchange reads skepticism as enacted postponement.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:99 supplies the direct correction: origination of heavens and earth establishes capacity to create their like. The inner “greatness” here is answered by an observed larger scale.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The imagined impossibility is answered at its source of form.** Lexical evidence: `ص د ر B004` (source from which forms issue) in `صُدُورِكُمْ`, `ع و د B001` (returning after departure) in `يُعِيدُنَا`, `ف ط ر B001` (opening and splitting) with `ف ط ر B002` (initiating into being) in `فَطَرَكُمْ`, and `ن غ ض B001` (head motion in astonishment) in `يُنْغِضُونَ`. Structural cue: 17:49–50 escalates from fragments to stone and iron, then this ayah lets the objectors posit whatever looms larger internally before returning to first origin; 17:52 converts the question into a responding summons. Assigned role: the chest generates the resistance-model, while originary splitting names a power prior to that form; head motion externalizes continued refusal. Abductive move: the first creation is supplied as answer; I infer that originating form from an opening includes power to return it after closure or dispersal. Reading change: the issue shifts from the present material's hardness to the more basic source-capacity that first differentiated and formed it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:52 converted the question “who returns us?” into an enacted call-and-answer, and 17:56 later reinforced that no alleged intermediary owns either removal or transformation.

baseline.text: Ya da gözünüzde daha da büyük olan başka bir yaratık olun. Bizi kim geri döndürecek, diyecekler. De ki: Sizi ilk kez yaratan. Sana başlarını sallayıp, Ne zaman olacak, diyecekler. De ki: Belki de yakındır.

findings.text: İçlerinde en büyük görünen yaratık bile ilk kez biçimi açıp var eden gücün ölçüsü olamaz; öznel büyüklük, yeniden yaratma kapasitesini sınırlamaz.
Baş sallama, direnci bedensel bir ertelemeye dönüştürürken “yakın” cevabı kuşkucunun koruduğu zaman mesafesini daraltır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P3 (17:40-60): Resistant Matter Reconstituted by a Summons
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Material disintegration and apparent hardness do not prevent a new formation when the originating power calls the dispersed subject back.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Resurrection is modeled as fresh measurement after cutting, while response functions like a piercing answer through apparently closed material.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Bone, Fragment, Stone, and Iron Remade
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Dispersed organic remains and resistant mineral bodies are all returned to a newly measured form by the originator.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hard bone (`quranic:root_001029:B005/m01`); pulverized remains (`quranic:root_000578:B001/m01`); solid stone (`quranic:root_000296:B003/m01`); resistant iron (`quranic:root_000002:B004/m01`); measuring a form (`quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`); originating existence (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); opening and splitting (`quranic:root_001165:B001/m01`); origination and beginning (`quranic:root_001165:B002/m01`); newness after cutting (`quranic:root_000227:B004/m01`); return after departure (`quranic:root_001058:B001/m01`); skeptical head-motion (`quranic:root_001526:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The objection moves from decay to maximal resistance, but both are placed inside the same productive operation. Creation is measurement and origination; newness itself carries the trace of a prior cut. The head's skeptical oscillation becomes a small bodily rehearsal of the return it denies.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, nesnenin kesilmesi ya da işlenmesi öncesinde ölçülmesini ve sınırlarının uygun biçimde belirlenmesini ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Deri örneği bu işlemi somutlaştırır; yoktan var etme ve yalan uydurma anlamları bu dalın parçası değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, eylemden önceki ölçme ve sınır belirleme aşamasıyla sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın ölçme ve biçme anlamını karşılar; başka dallardaki kalıplaşmış kullanımlar buraya taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir nesneyi kesme ya da uygulama öncesinde ölçüp sınırlarını uygun ve düzgün biçimde belirlemektir.

facets.statement: Nesnenin ölçüsü ve sınırları yapılacak işten önce belirlenir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Deri, kumaş veya benzeri bir nesnenin kesime hazırlanmasını anlatan bağlamlara uygundur.
